name: The Practice Toolkit
headline: Four tools. Ready for tomorrow morning.
intro: Training that helps your team use four trauma-informed tools in the moment, not just know them.

problem.scene: A child says "fine", then throws a mug.
problem.question: Your team knows what PACE stands for. What do they say next?
without: A consequence or a raised voice
Nobody has said the words out loud
with: Practised words for the hard moments
The same tool names at handover
problem.standards: Most teams have sat through trauma training. This course is mostly practice, out loud, on moments from your own setting.
problem.evidence: PACE keeps the boundary in place. Disclosures are never reframed: they go to the safeguarding lead that day.

groups: Residential support workers, team leaders and registered managers
Teaching assistants, pastoral staff and designated teachers
Lead practitioners and early help workers

outcomes: See it from the child's side
Describe a moment that escalated from the child's side, and how the adult's first words landed.
Recognise when a child you support is moving out of their window of tolerance.
Explain Siegel's window of tolerance and Perry's Regulate, Relate, Reason, and why reasoning fails in a hot moment.
Explain the four parts of PACE, and why accepting a feeling is not accepting the behaviour.
Use PACE and Spot, Soothe, Shift out loud, and know when a conversation has become a disclosure.
Choose the right tool for a moment from your own setting, and explain it in two sentences.

pillars.title: The four tools in The Practice Toolkit
pillars.stance: Tools you can use tomorrow morning
pillars.stance_line: A few minutes on the idea behind each tool, then most of the time on practice.
items: Spot the early signs that a child is leaving the zone where they can think and talk.
Lend your calm first. Questions and consequences come when the child can hear them.
Playfulness, acceptance, curiosity and empathy, with the boundary still in place.
Name the feeling, soothe it, then help the young person see it differently.
pillars.base: Built on Dan Siegel's window of tolerance, Bruce Perry's Regulate, Relate, Reason, Dan Hughes's PACE and John Gottman's emotion coaching.

story_line: Four stories run through the day: Zara, 15, Leon, 11, Freya, 8, and Ollie, 16. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

phone.title: Your PACE responses
phone.intro: Take the hardest thing a child has said to you. Rewrite your usual reply.
fields: "You're not my mum. You only do this for the money."
"That's not fair, after everything I do."
"It sounds like you're wondering if I really care."
"I wonder if bedtime is when you miss home most."
phone.key: Accept the feeling, not the behaviour. The boundary stays.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on trauma-informed practice, including Durham, where he put NVR into 11 children's homes and trained 120 residential staff, and Staffordshire, where four organisations trained 400 staff across health, social care and education together.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, so he knows what the standards expect of the adults around a child.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
